newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles may sue over welfare reform - board.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles may sue over welfare reform - board.

text.p: The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted on Tuesday to consider filing a lawsuit on behalf of legal immigrants challenging the constitutionality of federal welfare reform.

County supervisors voted 4-to-1 to consider filing their own lawsuit to prevent the federal government from cutting off legal immigrants from federal Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and food stamp benefits.
Over 90,000 disabled and elderly legal permanent residents in Los Angeles County face disqualification from the SSI program under federal welfare reform, the county said.
Under the new federal rules, an additional 105,000 legal residents of Los Angeles County will no longer be eligible for food stamps, the county said.
Last month, three lawsuits were filed in federal District Court challenging the constitutionality of the bar on legal immigrant access to SSI and food stamps.
At Tuesday's meeting, the Board of Supervisors asked county attorneys to review the three lawsuits and to report back in two weeks on the county's legal options.

Supervisors said they would consider filing their own lawsuit on behalf of legal immigrants, joining one of the three cases that have already been filed, or filing briefs in support of the existing lawsuits.
